prompt: Write balanced equations for the complete combustion of **(a)** magnesium and **(b)** propane.
Write an equation for the incomplete combustion of methane forming carbon monoxide, and explain why carbon monoxide is dangerous.
markscheme:
2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O **(A2)**

CO binds strongly to haemoglobin, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen; it is colourless and odourless **(R1)**

prompt: Compare coal and natural gas as fuels, giving one advantage of natural gas and one environmental disadvantage of coal.
markscheme:
Natural gas: cleaner burning, more energy per mole of CO₂ produced (higher H : C ratio), easy to transport by pipeline **(A1)**

Coal: produces the most CO₂ per unit energy **(A1)**, and impurities give SO₂ (acid rain) and particulates **(A1)**

prompt: Explain why biofuels such as bioethanol are described as renewable and, ideally, carbon-neutral, and give one limitation of this claim.
markscheme: The carbon released on burning was recently fixed by photosynthesis, so crops can be regrown in a short time **(R1)**; limitation: fossil fuels are used in farming, fertiliser, processing and transport, and land is taken from food production **(A1)**

prompt: For a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell in acid conditions, write the half-equations at each electrode and state one advantage over burning hydrogen.
markscheme:
Anode (oxidation): H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ **(A1)**; cathode (reduction): O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H₂O **(A1)**

Chemical energy is converted directly to electrical energy, so it is more efficient than combustion followed by a heat engine **(A1)**
